full_judgment:
In this revision Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 12-6-2022 (decree signed on 14-6-2022) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dinajpur in Other Class Appeal No. 45 of 2013 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 11-3-2013 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Hakimpur Dinjpur in Other Class Suit No. 29 of 2006 decreeing the suit should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner filed the suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the suit land stating that the suit land originally belonged to one Angari Mondol, CS Khatian No. 21, Plot No. 1177 measuring 1.20 acres and Plot No. 1108 measuring 1.00 acres totalling 2.20 acres of land stands recorded in his name. Angari Mondal died leaving behind two sons namely Rajob Ali Mondal and Monser Ali Mondal and two daughters namely Sutimon Nessa and Asimon Nessa as his legal heirs. At the time of SA record, one Uzir Ali fraudulently got his name recorded in SA Khatian No. 18. The heirs of Angari Mondal upon coming to know the matter filed Title Suit No. 176 of 1967 in the Munsif Court, Dinajpur Sadar and obtained a decree of title in respect of the suit land. Accordingly, SA khatian was corrected vide Case No. 219/27/83-84 and 13/03/90-91 and a new record being Khatian No. 18/1 was prepared in the name of the heirs of said Angari Mondal. By a deed of amicable partition, the suit properties fell in the share of Monser Ali who had been possessing the same exclusively. Monser Ali Mondal died leaving wife Amisa Bewa, one son Elias Ali and three daughters Saleha Khatun, Akjahan Bibi and Banesa Bibi as his heirs. The plaintiff-petitioner got the suit land in his share by a compromise agreement with his sisters and since then, he has been possessing the land by cultivating the same. On 30-8-2006, the defendant No. 1 claimed title to the suit land and hence, the petitioner filed the instant suit. Subsequently, the defendant No. 21 has been added who had purchased the suit land measuring 1.271/2 acres of land from defendants on different dates. 

3. Defendant Nos. 3 and 4 filed written statement supporting the case of the plaintiff. Added defendant No. 21 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material facts stated in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to one Angari Mondol which was recorded in his name in CS Khatian No. 21. Angari Mondol died leaving behind two sons Rajob Ali Mondol and Monser Ali Mondol and two daughters Sutimon Nessa and Asimon Nessa as his legal heirs. Thereafter, Khatian No. 18/1 was prepared in the name of the heirs of Angari Mondal. Rajob Ali Mondal died leaving behind three sons namely Iqbal, Aslam and Md. Islam and four daughters namely Kajeman Bibi, Mahila Begum, Aklima and Afroza Bewa i.e. Proforma defendant Nos. 2-8 as his heirs. Monser Ali Mondal died leaving behind his wife Amisa Bewa, one son Elias Ali and three daughters Saleha Begum, Akjahan Bibi and Banesa Bibi, Proforma defendant Nos. 9-12 as his heirs. Sutimon Nessa alias Putli, daughter of Angari Mondal died leaving behind her husband namely Alimuddin, one son Mozahar Ali and daughter Mirjan Bibi, proforma defendant Nos. 13-14 in suit. Asimon Nessa, daughter of Angari Mondal died leaving son Md. Kalam and two daughters Pochimon Nessa and Hazra Bewa, Proforma defendant Nos. 15-17. 

4. The defendant No. 21 purchased 40 decimals of land from defendant No. 15 vide registered deed No. 270 dated 27-1-2008, 61/2 decimals of land from defendant No. 16 vide registered deed No. 272 dated 27-1-2008, 34 decimals of land from defendant No. 17 vide registered deed No. 271 dated 27-1-2008, 05 decimals of land from defendant No. 2 vide registered deed No. 327 dated 28-1-2008 and 15 decimals of land from defendant No. 13 vide registered deed No. 341 dated 3-2-2008 and registered deed No. 378 and 70 dated 3-3-2008. The defendant No. 21 purchased in total 1.271/2 acres of land vide six deeds from the aforementioned proforma defendants and since then, the defendant No. 21 has been in possessing the same. 

5. The learned trial court framed as many as four issues in disposing of the instant suit. The plaintiff examined four PWs to prove his case and adduced documentary evidence which were marked as exhibit Nos. 1-10. The defendant No. 21 examined three DWs and furnished documents which were duly marked as exhibit Nos. "Ka-Da". The trial court after hearing by its judgment and decree dated 11-3-2013 decreed the suit. 

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the defendant No. 21 filed Other Class Appeal No. 45 of 2013 before the District Judge, Dinajpur. Eventually, the said appeal was transferred to the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dinajpur, for hearing and disposal who after hearing by the impugned judgment and decree dated 12-6-2022 allowed the appeal and thereby set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. At this juncture, the petitioner moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule. 

7. Mr. Md. Mahabubur Rashid with Mr. Md. Munsur Rahman. learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner submits that before the trial court all the PWs as well as defendant Nos. 3 and 4 unequivocally admitted that the property in question inherited by the petitioner from his father and by amicable arrangement among other co-sharers, he got the same in his share exclusively and has been possessing the same with the knowledge and consent of other co-sharer-defendants. 

8. He submits that the suit was filed in fact against the defendant No. 1 who had no connection with the suit property as he is not a co-sharer by inheritance. Other co-sharer have been made as pro-forma defendants. When the suit was proceeding towards hearing, all of a sudden defendant No. 21 came into scene and claimed title in the suit property by purchase during pendency of the suit and got him added as defendant No. 21. 

9. He submits that evidences led by the plaintiff established that none of the pro-forma defendants were in possession of the suit property and they never raised claim in the suit land, but the defendant No. 21 with mala fide intention somehow managed to create some sale deeds from some of the pro-forma defendants who had no title and possession in the property. The defendant No. 21 got no possession of the property alleged to have been purchased by him on the basis of a bainanama allegedly executed on 5-6-2005, which has been created by the defendant No. 21 on the stamp purchased in the name of one Md. Iqbal Hossain who is neither executant nor purchaser. The trial court rightly held that the bainanama has been created by erasing signature of some person on the stamp paper. 

10. He also argued that had it been executed by the vendor of the defendant No. 21, it would have been mentioned in the recital of the sale deed, but nothing stated in the deed about execution of any bainanama by the vendor. The trial court also observed that in the event of transfer of property by any of the defendants in suit during pendency is hit by section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, and unless the defendant No. 21 can establish title from pro-forma defendants by purchase in an independent suit, the deeds in question cannot create any title in favour of the defendant. 

11. He finally argued that the defendant as per his deed of sale purchased the property from SA Khatian No. 702, but in the instant case the plaintiff claimed the properties under CS Khatia No. 21 and corrected khatian No. 18/1. The trial court upon consideration of evidences both oral and documentary found exclusive possession of the plaintiff in the suit property and also observed that nothing has come out on cross from the PWs. Moreover, pro-forma defendant Nos. 3 and 4 co-sharers of the plaintiff admitted that the plaintiff acquired right, title and possession in the suit property exclusively by amicable arrangement among all the co-sharers, but the appellate court while allowing the appeal and remanding the suit to the trial court for fresh trial wrongly observed that the dispute between the parties is whether the plaintiff's father acquired title exclusively in the suit property by amicable arrangement among the co-sharers and whether he got exclusive possession of the property completely ousting other co-sharers from the suit land and by that act whether the plaintiff acquired any title in the property without bringing a suit for partition. Where co-sharer defendant Nos. 3 and 4 supported the case of the plaintiff by filing written statement, that father of the plaintiff got the suit property amicably of his share and after his death all the heirs inherited the same and among the plaintiff also absolutely got the property in his share by amicable arrangement among them, there is no need for bringing any suit for partition unless the co-sharer in the property could prove their possession in any portion of the land. In the instant case none of the co-sharer defendants came forward by filing written statement to claim that there was no amicable partition and they are in possession as co-sharer. In the absence of such claim of the co-sharer defendants, the appellate court ought not to have allowed the appeal and sent the case back to the trial court on remand for fresh trial. As such, the appellate court has committed an error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

12. Mr. Ehsan A Siddiq with Mr. Imran A Siddiq, Mr. Chowdhury Ishrak, Ahmed Siddiky, Mr. Mohammad Shahnewaz and Ms. Shadia Afrin Jeny, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite party No. 1 submit that the plaintiff categorically stated that the property originally belonged to one Angari Mondal who died leaving two sons and two daughters who inherited the property. The plaintiff is one of the heirs of Monser Ali Mondal. After the death of Monser Ali plaintiff and his mother and three sisters inherited the property and claimed that by amicable partition among the heirs of Monser Ali he exclusively got the property in his share. The defendants did not deny the share of Monser Ali Mondal inherited from Angari Mondal, but the defendant No. 21 claimed that the plaintiff failed to show any evidence either oral or documentary that Monser Ali Mondal got the property by amicable partition or after his death Elias Ali also got the property in his share by any deed or any evidence. In the absence of any written instrument as admitted by the plaintiff all the heirs of Angari Mondal are co-sharer in the property. Possession of a co-sharer in the property, does not mean that he is owner of the property of other co-sharers, but according to law a co-sharer in possession means that he has been possessing the property for and on behalf of other co-sharers, unless he could prove that his possession is adversed to other co-sharer by any act and conduct. In the instant suit no such evidence has come forward to establish the exclusive title in the property of the plaintiff ousting other co-sharer of the property. 

13. He submits that the trial court while decreeing the suit criticized the bainanama as well as six sale deeds in their entirety and found that the bainanama was created by the defendant No. 21 in connivance with the some of the proforma defendants on 211 antidated stamp, but failed to find that when a registered sale deed executed and registered in favour of the purchaser by the owner of the property, there was no validity of the bainanama entered in between the purchaser and the vendor earlier. A bainama is a contract by which the vendor promises to sell the property to the purchaser and pursuant to such promise, the purchaser made part payment out of the total consideration. Therefore, for determination of the dispute between the parties, the alleged bainanama is not a major factor which contributes nothing in the merit of the suit. 

14. He argued that admittedly defendant No. 21 purchased some of the property from co-sharers of the plaintiff by different deeds and after purchase he got his name mutated in the khatian. When the defendant No. 21 purchased some of the property from co-sharer of the plaintiff, title of the plaintiff has become clouded, as such, to determine the validity of the deed of the defendant No. 21 and claim of entire suit property by the plaintiff all the co-sharers and all the properties left by Angari Mondal are required to be included into hotchpot. Only taking a portion of the property left by Angari Mondal, it cannot be determined whether there was any amicable arrangement among the co-sharer and what was the quantum of land left by Angari Mondal obtained by other co-sharers. One of the co-sharer cannot claim title over the suit land without bringing all the properties left by Angari Mondal into hotchpot. Therefore, the appellate court rightly held that to get the dispute properly adjudicated upon instant case for simple declaration is not at all maintainable without a prayer for partition of the property and for that reason to enable the plaintiff to get his relief properly adjudicated, giving an opportunity to get his plaint properly amended and to adduce sufficient evidences before the trial court thought it wise and necessary for the interest of justice to sent the case back to the trial court on remand for fresh trial. 

15. He submits that under section 107 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the appellate court has power to remand the case to the trial court if it finds that the important issue has not been decided properly or the material fact on the part of both the parties have not been incorporated in the pleading. In the instant case, the appellate court rightly found that unless the plaintiff brought a suit for partition along with declaration of title, mere declaration of title in the property will not properly determine the dispute between the parties, as such, the appellate court has not committed any error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

16. He finally argued that the trial court without any relief sought for by the plaintiff, unfortunately observed that all the sale deeds of the defendant No. 21 are void and inoperative and by the said deed, the defendant No. 21 acquired no title in the property, but failed to find that how the plaintiff acquired exclusive title in the property without partition of the suit property. 

17. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, have gone through the revisional application, plaint in suit, written statement, evidences both oral and documentary and the impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below. 

18. The plaintiff claimed that admittedly, owner of the property was one Angari Mondal. CS khatian stands recorded in his name, who died leaving sons Rajob Ali Mondal, Monser Ali Mondal and daughters Sutimon Nesa ancl Asimon Nessa. Rajob Ali died leaving three sons defendant Nos. 2-4, four daughters Kajeman Bibi, Most. Aklima, Mahila Begum and Afroza Bewa (defendant Nos. 5-8). Monser Ali Mondal died leaving son Elias Ali, the plaintiff, wife Amisa Bewa, defendant No. 9, daughter Saleha Khaun, Akjahan Bibi and Banesa Bibi (defendant Nos. 10-12). Said Asimon Nessa died leaving son Md. Mozahar Ali and daughter Mirjan Bibi (defendant No. 13 and 14), Sutimon Nessa died leaving son Abut Kalam daughter Pochimon Nessa and Most. Hazra Bewa, defendant Nos. 15-17. The plaintiffs claimed that among the heirs of Angari Mondal his father Monser Ali Mondal got the suit property exclusively in his share by amicable partition and while in exclusive possession and enjoyment died leaving plaintiff and defendant Nos. 9-12, again there has been an amicable partition/arrangement among the heirs of Monser Ali Mondal and by such arrangement he got the property exclusively in his share and has been possessing the same with the knowledge of other co-sharers ousting them for more than statutory period of limitation. 

19. It is also claimed that admitting the fact two sons of Rajob Ali Mondal named Md. Aslam Ali and Md. Islam Ali (defendant Nos. 3 and 4) filed written statement and in support of their written statement, defendant No. 3 Aslam Ali deposed before the trial court who was cross examined by the defendant No. 1 but nothing found on cross examination in favour of the defendant. Therefore, the plaintiff could able to prove that from the time of his father he has been possessing the suit property as exclusive owner of the same. Accordingly, in the recent field survey the property in question has been recorded in his name. 

20. The defendant No. 21 by filing written statement claimed that he purchased 40 decimals of land from defendant No. 15 by deed No. 270 dated 27-1-2008, 61/2 decimals of land from defendant No. 16 by a registered deed No. 272 dated 27-1-2008, 34 sataks of land from defendant No. 17 by registered deed No. 271 dated 27-1-2008, 5 decimals of land from defendant No. 2 by registered deed No. 327 dated 28-1-2008 and 15 decimals of land from defendant No. 13 by registered deed No. 341 dated 3-2-2008 and deed Nos. 378 and 70 dated 3-3-2008. In the manner aforesaid by six sale deeds the defendant No. 21 purchased in total 1.27½ acres of land from pro-forma defendants who are co-sharer in the suit land. 

21. Only claim of the plaintiff that he got the property exclusively in his share by way of amicable arrangement among the heirs of Angari Mondal and then among the heirs of Manser Ali, but no such arrangement has come before the court to substantiate the claim of the plaintiff. From plaint, it is also not found that how amicable arrangement among the heirs of Angari Mondal was done and which property in exchange of the suit property was given in the share of other co-sharers. The plaintiff also could not show how he acquired the property exclusively excluding other heirs of Monser Ali. If we concede that the property acquired by Monser Ali by inheritance and left by him devolved upon all his heirs and among them the mother and sister amicably relinquished their claim in favour of the plaintiff, in that case, in the absence of any amicable arrangement among the heirs of Angari Mondal, Monser Ali can claim 1/3rd share in the property left by his father. The suit Plot Nos. 1177 measuring 1.20 acres and 1108 measuring 1 acre totalling 2.20 acres claimed by the plaintiff only on the basis of an amicable arrangement among the heirs. 

22. The trial court in decreeing the suit has taken into consideration oral evidences led by the plaintiff saying that the property amicably fell in the share of the plaintiff. Had the property amicably partitioned among the co-sharers, question may arise why other co-sharer should transfer their share in favour of defendant No. 21. In the absence of any legal instrument in writing it cannot be construed that other co-sharers relinquished their share in favour of the plaintiff or his father Monser Ali in exchange of having their share from other property left by Angari Modal. 

23. The trial court further held that bainanama (Exhibit-Tha) has not been registered as per section 17A of Registration Act, and the said bainanama is invalid, subsequently created on the stamp purchased by one Md. Iqbal Hossain and also observed that it was written on stamp signed by some other person by erasing signature of somebody. 

24. I find that the observation regarding execution of the bainanama to some extent true, but this bainanama is not subject matter of the suit. As such, all the observations made by the trial court in respect of execution of bainanama, registration of the same, filing of a suit for Specific performance of Contract are redundant for determination of the dispute between the parties, moreover, bainanama in question was not required to be registered on the date of its execution. In the instant case only question to be decided by the court whether a co-sharer by filing a suit for simple declaration of title on the basis of amicable arrangement among the co-sharer without any written instrument and bringing all other property left by their predecessor into hotchpot can claim title exclusively without filing a suit for partition. 

25. The trial court did not touch the said question and only relying on the evidence of PWs and one of the DWs came into a finding that the defendant acquired no title in the property by purchase from other co-sharer-defendants, as the bainanama has been created later on to show a contract for sale much earlier than the filing of the suit and said bainanama was required to be registered under the Registration Act, and khatian number mentioned in the sale deed is wrong not attracting the suit property under Khatian No. 18/1. 

26. From perusal of six sale deeds of defendant No. 21, it appears that the suit property sold by other co-sharers to the defendant No. 21 covered by Plot Nos. 1177 and 1108 showing the property under Khatian No. 702. the defendant filed certified copy of the said khatian before the trial court nothing could bring by the plaintiff in evidence that the khatian No. 702 filed by the defendant (Exhibit-Ka) is forged and fabricated. Moreover, it appears that the same stands recorded in the name of Rajob Ali Mondal, Monser Ali Mandol along with others, in conformity with the (Exhibit-4) filed by the plaintiff showing khatian No. 18/1 stands corrected pursuant to judgment and decree passed by the 2nd Munsif Court, Dinajpur Sadar in Case No. 176 of 1967, existence of the same unequivocally admitted by both the parties. Mere difference of khatian number cannot make a sale deed invalid if the quantum of land, plot number, owner of the property and the vendors are not challenged by other parties. 

27. The trial court ought to have found that a co-sharer by filing a simple suit for declaration of title for particular quantum of land without partition of the same is not at all entitled to get proper relief. The appellate court while allowing the appeal in its judgment held that; 
"তর্কিত রায় ও নথি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, স্বীকৃত মতেই নালিশী জমিতে যেমন বাদী/রেসপনডেন্ট এর স্বত্ব আছে তেমনি বিবাদীগনেরও স্বত্ব আছে তবে কোন পক্ষ কতটুকু সম্পত্তিতে স্বত্ববান তা বাটোয়ারা ব্যতীত সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করা সম্ভব নহে। যেহেতু 'ক' তফসিল বর্নিত নালিশী সম্পত্তিসহ আরও সম্পত্তি বাদী ও বিবাদীগণের পূর্বাধিকারী আঙ্গারী মন্ডলের ছিল সেহেতু আঙ্গারী মন্ডলের নামীয় সকল সম্পত্তি তার ওয়ারিশদের মধ্যে আইনগতভাবে বন্টিত না হওয়া পর্যন্ত তার জের ওয়ারিশগনকে কি পরিমান জমি কোন দাগে ও খতিয়ানে প্রাপ্ত হবে তা নির্ধারণ করা সম্ভব নহে। আঙ্গারী মন্ডলের সমুদয় জমি আইনগত ভাবে তার জের ওয়ারিশদের মধ্যে বন্টন হওয়া অপরিহার্য ছিল। কাজেই বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত বাটোয়ারার প্রার্থনা ব্যতীত শুধুমাত্র স্বত্ব ঘোষনার প্রার্থনায় আনীত অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি বর্তমান আকারে প্রকারে রক্ষণীয় মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করে ভ্রমে পতিত হয়েছেন। তর্কিত রায় ও নথি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত বাদী/আপীল্যান্টপক্ষের নালিশী জমিতে স্বত্ব ও দখল আছে মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করলেও বাদী ইলিয়াছ আলী কিভাবে তার পিতা মনছের আলীর সমুদয় সম্পত্তির মালিক ও স্বতবান হলেন তার কোন ব্যাখ্যা তার রায়ে উল্লেখ করেন নাই কারন বাদীর স্বীকৃতমতেই তার সহোদর বোন ও মা তার পিতা মারা গেলে ওয়ারিশ বিদ্যমান আছে। কাজেই নালিশী জমিতে প্রকৃতপক্ষে বাদী ইলিয়াছ আলীর কি পরিমান জমিতে স্বত্ব আছে তা বাটোয়ারা ব্যতিত সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান সম্ভব নহে। অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি স্বত্বসহ বাটোয়ারার প্রার্থনায় আনয়ন করা অপরিহার্য ছিল। প্রকৃতপক্ষে নালিশী 'ক' তপসিল বর্ণিত জমিতে কে কি পরিমান প্রাপ্ত হবে তা বাটোয়ারা ব্যতীত শুধুমাত্র স্বত্ব ঘোষনার প্রার্থনায় অত্র মোকদ্দমায় নির্ধারন করা সমীচীন নহে। কাজেই নালিশী 'ক' তফসিল বর্ণিত জমিসহ বাদী ও বিবাদীগনের পূর্বাধিকারী আঙ্গারী মন্ডলের সমুদয় সম্পত্তির আইনগতভাবে বন্টন ব্যতীত শুধুমাত্র স্বত্ব ঘোষনার ডিক্রি প্রদান করে বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত ভুল করেছেন ফলে তা হস্তক্ষেপযোগ্য হচ্ছে।"

28. Above observations made by the appellate court found to be in consonance with the provision of law and by sending the suit to the trial court on remand for fresh trial, committed no error of law rather the court afforded opportunity to the plaintiff to get the suit properly adjudicated upon suitably amending his plaint and bringing all the property left by Angari Mondal into hotchpot. In the event of proving that other co-sharers got their respective share from other non-suited property left by Angari Mondal in exchange of suit property with the plaintiff by amicable arrangement the plaintiff will succeed and for the reason of remand of the suit, the plaintiff has not in any way deprived from his right, but he will get sufficient opportunity to get his pleading suitably amended and adduce evidences in support of his claim. This question would not have come for adjudication of the present suit if all the co-sharer defendants admitted the claim of the plaintiff like defendant Nos. 3 and 4, but other defendants claiming their title as co-sharers in the property during pendency of the suit transferred some property to the defendant No. 21 which indicates that all the co-sharers did not surrender their share in favour of plaintiff or his father Monser Ali. 

29. Since some of the co-sharers claiming title in the property transferred the same to the defendant No. 21, title of the co-sharer in the property and validity and legality of their transfer in favour of defendant No. 21 is required to be adjudicated upon in the present suit. For that reason unless all the property left by Angari Mondal is brought into hotchpot simply two plots in its entirety cannot be given to a person who is a co-sharer, in the absence of any partition deed. In a similar situation, the apex court in the case of Tayeb Ali vs Abdul Khalek and others in Civil Appeal No. 42 of 1985 held that, 
"the suit being one for declaration of title to an unspecified share of an undivided plot of land and there being no evidence of exclusive possession at any time, the present suit is not maintainable without a prayer for partition". 

30. In the case of Majeda Khatun and others vs Jiban Nessa and others reported in 62 DLR (AD) 239, held that; 
"the appellate court exercise in its power under section 107 can make an order of remand if it is so required for full and effective adjudication of all the relevant points involve in a case, but no remand order can however be made to facilitated to fill up the lacuna in his case". 

31. In the instant case, the question of filling up any lacuna cannot come, rather, the appellate court by sending the suit to the trial court on remand facilitated an opportunity to the plaintiff to get proper relief. In the case of Chan Miah (Md) and others vs Md. Shamsuddin and others in Civil Appeal No. 56 of 1993, it is held that; 
"the appellate court found fault with the finding of possession arises by the trial court holding that the reason of the trial court suffered from discrepancies and also found that the Assistant Custodian of Vested Property was necessary party and sent back the case on remand for deciding it on all points after fresh trial. Such an order on the fact and in the circumstances of the case has not cause any miscarriage of justice for any patent illegality as such". 

32. In the instant case also the appellate court by sending the suit on remand to the trial court has not done any injustice to the plaintiff. Therefore, it would not be proper for this Court in exercising revisional jurisdiction to interfere with the order of remand. A defendant in suit during pendency of litigation if transfers any property in favour of any other person hit by section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, but in the instant case as admitted by plaintiff, the defendants are co-sharer in the property who relinquished their share amicably in favour of the plaintiff and his father. Therefore, the defendant No. 21 is an assignee. Accordingly, an assignee can be made party in the suit by filing an application for addition of party. Accordingly, the defendant No. 21 added as assignee in the suit. Therefore, when the plaintiff accepted his joining in the suit as one of the defendants and allowed him to contest the suit the plaintiff ought to have taken recourse to a suit for partition by bringing all the properties into hotchpot. 

33. Therefore, I find no error in the decision of the appellate court calling for interference by this Court. 

34. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs. 

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned and send down the lower court records at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule, under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, was issued in the following term — 
"Record of the case be called for and let a Rule issue calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 14-5-2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rajshahi in Title Appeal No. 197 of 2002 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming those dated 28-5-2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Durgapur, Rajshahi in Title Suit No. 11 of 1996 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this Court stayed all further proceedings of the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-5-2002 for 3(three) months from the date and lastly, it was extended on 10-1-2005 for a period of another 6(six) months from the date. 

3. The present opposite parties as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 11 of 1996 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Durgapur, Rajshahi against the present petitioners as the defendants for a decree of permanent injunction in respect of the suit land. 

4. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to one Amin Mondol, and the CS record was prepared in his name. He sold 1.31 acres of land from Sabek Plot No. 2232 to Taser Sorder on 19-7-1958 and then he sold out the land of Sabek Plot Nos. 1200 and 1844 to Arjan Bibi on 13-3-1959 and accordingly, the SA Khatian No. 142 and RS Khatian No. 380 were duly recorded in their names jointly. Thereafter, Taser Sorder on 23-7-1976, sold 1.31 acres of land to Zarman who then on 24-10-1982, sold the same to Abdul Barek, who on 10-7-1988, transferred his purchased land to plaintiff Nos. 1-3 by way of registered deed. Subsequently. Taser Sarder sold 0.40 acres of land of Sabek plot No.1844 to Rahman Sarder and Abdul Latif. Rahman Sarder sold his share to Abdul Hamid on 02-8-1982, and then Abdul Hamid on 30-9-1989, sold 0.20 acres of land from the western side of the said plot to plaintiff Nos. 4-6. Thereafter, Abdul Latif on 20-8-1982 sold his share of 0.20 acres of land to one Rostom Ali who then on 15-10-1988 exchanged the said land with plaintiff No. 7 Moyjuddin. Plaintiff No. 8 has been possessing 0.76 acres of the scheduled land since his purchase. The defendants threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess them from the suit land on 15-1-1996, and hence the suit. 

5. The defendants contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the averments made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Taser Sorder purchased 1.31 acres of land from Sabek plot No.2232 from Amin Mondal vide registered Kabala No. 15115 dated 19-8-1958, and similarly, his wife Arjan Bibi purchased 0.40 acres from Sabek plot No. 1844; 0.76 acres from Sabek plot No. 2303 and 0.35 acres from Sabek plot No. 4751 in total 1.51 acres of land by a registered Kabala dated 10-3-1959, and at the time of SA's operation, the said in total 2.82 acres of land were recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 142. Aijan Bibi sold 0.35 acres of land to one Oazed Ali and Adam Ali before the RS operation. The remaining 2.47 acres of land were recorded in RS Khatian No. 380 in their names in ejmali. They were issueless. Taser Sorder died before his wife. After the death of Arjan Bibi her brother Munsad, and sister Nurjahan became the lawful heirs and owned and possessed the land left by their sister Arjan Bibi. Thereafter, they sold 0.40 acres of land to the defendants by registered Kabala deeds on 02-3-1996 (Exhibit-Ka and Kha) and handed over possession to them and they are enjoying the property. 

6. After the conclusion of the trial the learned Assistant Judge, Durgapur, Rajshahi by his judgment and decree dated 28-5-2002 decreed the suit on the contest against the defendants without cost and restrained the defendants by way of a permanent injunction so that they could not disturb the peaceful enjoying of the plaintiff in the suit land. 7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree dated 28-5-2002 the defendants as the appellants preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, Rajshahi, and the same was numbered Title Appeal No. 197 of 2002. Thereafter, the appeal was transferred before the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court; Rajshahi who after hearing the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 14-5-2003 
disallowed the appeal on the contest without cost by affirming those of the Trial Court. 

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said impugned judgment and decree dated 14-5-2003 the defendants as the petitioners had preferred this civil revision before this Court and obtained the instant Rule which is before us for consideration. 

9. Anyway, Mr. Md. Shariful Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendants-petitioners submits that both the Courts below committed an error of law in holding the view that the defendants failed to file any separate Khatian or Dakhila in the name of Arjan Bibi, and on the other hand, during the lifetime of Arjan Bibi her husband Taser Sorder sold 0.40 acres of land, and if there were no amicable settlement between the husband and wife, Arjan Bibi ought to have filed a suit for cancellation of the deed executed by her husband but she did not, take any initiative to that effect. Besides, Taser Sorder was the sharer of 01 anna in his wife Arjan Bibi's land, as such, his said transfer was legal. The Courts below also held that since the defendants claimed purchasing the land from the heirs of said Arjan Bibi they had the option to file a partition suit if they desire so. 

10. He further submits that the Courts below failed to consider that Taser Sorder purchased 1.31 acres of land from Sabek plot No.2232 from Amin Mondal vide registered Kabala No. 15115 dated 19-8-1958, and similarly, his wife Arjan Bibi purchased 0.40 acres from Sabek plot No. 1844; 0.76 acres from Sabek plot No. 2303 and 0.35 acres from Sabek plot No. 4751 in. total 1.51 acres of land by a registered Kabala dated 10-3-1959, and at the time of SA's operation, the said in total 2.82 acres of land were recorded in SA Khatian No. 142. Arjan Bibi sold 0.35 acres of land to one Wazed Ali and Adam Ali before RS Operation. The remaining 2.47 acres of land were recorded in RS Khatian No. 380 in their names in ejmali. They were issueless. Taser Sorder died before his wife. After the death of Arjan Bibi her brother Munsad, and sister Nurjahan became the lawful heirs and owned and possessed the land left by their sister Arjan Bibi. Thereafter, they sold 0.40 acres of land to the defendants by registered Kabala and handed over possession to them. 

11. He lastly submits that both the Courts below failed to consider that the instant suit for a permanent injunction is not maintainable in an undivided ejmali property and the findings are not based on the proper assessment of the materials on record which occasioned a failure of justice. 

12. Conversely, Mr. Abul Kashem Bhuiyan the learned Advocate appearing with Mr. Raihan Kawsar, Advocate on behalf of the plaintiffs-opposite parties submits that both the Courts below considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record rightly decreed the suit on concurrent findings and thereby committed no illegality occasioning a failure of justice. 

13. He next submits that in a suit for a permanent injunction, the plaintiff is required to prove his exclusive possession over the suit land and a prima facie title thereto as the Court cannot decide the title in a simple suit for a permanent injunction. In the instant suit, the plaintiffs could able to prove their conclusive possession over the suit land and prima facie title thereto as such; both the Courts below rightly decreed the suit of the plaintiffs and thereby committed no illegality. He lastly submits that there is no misreading and non-consideration of the material facts on record or error of law to have been committed in passing the impugned judgment and decree. 

14. Heard the learned Advocates of the contending parties and have perused the materials on record. It appears that the plaintiffs filed the instant suit for a decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing their peaceful enjoyment of the suit land. The plaintiff prayed for injunction over 2.47 acres of land and the defendants undeniably accepted the plaintiffs' title and possession over the suit land except for 40 decimals of the land of S.A plot No. 1844 and RS plot No. 2438 claiming that after the death of Arjan Bibi issuless her brother and sister became her legal heirs and sold out said 40 decimals of land to defendant Nos. 2 and 3 on 02-3-1996 by way of registered Kabala deeds (Exhibits-Ka and Kha), that is to say, after filing the instant suit on 15-1-1996 and during the pendency of the same by which the defendants did not acquire any title over the said land and possession thereon. It also appears that Taser Sarder and his wife Arjan Bibi were the owners of said 40 decimals of land on equal share by purchase and SA Khatian No.142 and RS Khatian No.380 (Exhibits-I and II) were prepared in their names as husband and wife in ejmali and during their title and possession over the land Taser Ali amicably sold out the said 40 decimals of land to one Rahman Sarder and Abdul Latif on 31-3-1973 who subsequently transferred the land to different persons from whom the plaintiffs got the same by purchase and exchange in 1988/1989 and entered into possession. There is no such evidence that Arjan Bibi ever raised any objection about the said sale of her ejmali land by her husband during her lifetime, from which it appears that the plaintiffs could able to prove their prima facie title over the suit land. On perusal of the evidence on record, it also appears that the plaintiffs were able to prove their exclusive possession over the suit land by oral and documentary evidence. The defendants threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess them from the suit land before execution of their (defendants) alleged deeds (Exhibits-Ka and Kha). In the circumstances, both the Courts below considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record rightly decreed the suit of the plaintiffs on concurrent findings and thereby committed no illegality occasioning failure of justice. However, concurrent findings of the Courts below cannot be interfered with unless there is a misreading or non-consideration of the material facts on record or an error of law to have been committed in passing the impugned judgment and decree. But in the case at hand, I do not find any such misreading or non-consideration of the material facts available on record or any error of law. 

15. In the course of submissions, Mr. Bhuiyan referred to the decision in the case of Md. Kamal and others vs AKM Mohsin and others reported in 10 MLR (AD) (2005) 100 wherein in paragraph Nos. 6 and 7 it was held that — 
"On perusal of the judgment of the trial Court, it appears that the trial Court has arrived at a finding of exclusive possession with prima facie title of the plaintiff in the suit land. The Court of Appeal below though not discussed the evidence on the record but has agreed with the finding of the trial Court. The High Court Division, however, refused to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below holding that the trial Court discussed the evidence of both the parties, oral and documentary, in arriving at a finding that the plaintiff has a prima facie title and exclusive possession in the suit land and that the appellate Court while affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court is not required to reassess the oral evidence with minute details. The High Court Division further held that in response to the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that PW 3 Abdur Rahman having introduced the new story to the effect that Abdur Rahman purchased the land from the plaintiff subsequently to institution the suit and has been in possession after his purchase was not permissible under provision of Order 6 rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure and observed as under: 
Having judged this particular provision of law, from such angle of vision, I find in the instant case the plaintiffs having introduced their case to the effect that they have been in possession of the suit land in exercise of their title therein and in view of subsequent development namely transfer of some land out of the suit land in favour of PW 3 Abdur Rahman the evidence was led at the stage of trial to the effect that Abdur Rahman being subsequent purchaser as also being constituted attorney of the remaining suit land on behalf of the plaintiffs had been exercising his right or possession over the same and such evidence even if led at the stage of trial by the plaintiff it can neither be said to be inconsistent with their previous pleading nor the same can be termed as a new ground of claim since Abdur Rahman PW 3 is none but a person stepping into the shoes of the plaintiffs and none else. Under such circumstances, I hold that the decisions relied on by the learned Advocate for the petitioners are not applicable in the instant case.' (Para-6)" 
"The suit is one for permanent injunction and the essential feature of the suit is to ascertain the exclusive possession of the suit land and in deciding the said issue the Court could incidentally go into the title if the same is inextricably mixed up with the question of possession while enquiring into the respective claims of the parties to the suit for determining whether the plaintiff is in exclusive possession of the disputed property and is entitled to a decree for permanent injunction. This view finds support in the case of Rafizuddin Ahmed vs Mongla Barnum and others reported in 43 DLR (AD) 215 wherein it has been held that: 
"In a simple suit for permanent injunction with regard to a disputed landed property, the relief is available to a person who is in possession. The Court may enquire incidentally into the respective claims of the parties to the suit for determining whether the plaintiff has got a prima facie case i.e., whether he is in possession of the disputed property and entitled to the specific relief of permanent injunction. If the dispute involves complicated questions of title the plaintiff must establish his title by filing a regular suit for declaration of title. A simple suit for permanent injunction should not be allowed to be used as a testing device for ascertainment of title.' (Para-7)" 

16. In the attending facts and circumstances of the case, the above-cited decision is squarely applicable to the case at hand. 

17. Given the above, I do not find any substance in the submissions so made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners, rather; find substance in the submissions made by the learned. Advocate for the opposite parties. Accordingly, the Rule fails. 

18. As a result, the Rule is discharged without cost. 

19. Stay, if any, vacated. 

20. The impugned judgment and decree dated 14-5-2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Rajshahi in Title Appeal No. 197 of 2002 disallowing the appeal by affirming those dated 28-5-2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Durgapur, Rajshahi in Title Suit No. 11 of 1996 decreeing the suit is hereby upheld. 

Send a copy of this judgment along with the LCR to the Court below at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 14-6-2021 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No. 126 of 2018 allowing the Civil Revision and setting-aside the order dated 25-4-2018 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 9 of 2005 staying the proceedings of the Execution Case should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Relevant facts, in short, are that the Opposite party No.1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 117 of 1999 in the Court of the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for specific performance of contract. 

3. Ultimately, the said suit was dismissed by the judgment and decree dated 27-2-2003. Against which the plaintiff-petitioners took an appeal being Title Appeal No. 198 of 2003 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which was subsequently transmitted to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge for disposal, who allowed the appeal on the basis of solenama by Judgment and decree dated 9-11-2005 and thereafter, the decree holder plaintiff to execute the decree filed Title Execution Case No. 9 of 2005. 

4. In this backdrop, the present petitioners filed Title Suit No. 4278 of 2008 challenging the sole decree before the learned Joint District Judge and Arbitration Court, which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 363 of 2016 and the said suit was dismissed for default. Thereafter, the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No.10 of 2017 for restoration of the said suit which is still pending. 

5. While the said execution case No. 9 of 2005 was in progress the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 363 of 2016 filed an application before the executing Court under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceedings of the Execution Case No. 9 of 2005 till disposal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2017 in the court of the, learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court Dhaka. 

6. The learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court after hearing the parties by his order dated 25-3-2018 stayed all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 9 of 2005 till disposal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2010 arising out of a default order passed in Title Suit No. 363 of 2016. 

7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 25-3-2018 the defendants filed Civil Revision No. 126 of 2018 before the learned District Judge which was subsequently transmitted to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for disposal, who after hearing the parties by the impugned judgment and order dated 14-6-2021 allowed the Civil Revision and set-aside the order passed by the executing Court on the findings that—
"উল্লেখ্য যে, দরখাস্তকারী ১-৬ নং প্রতিপক্ষ উক্ত ডিক্রীজারী ৯/২০০৫ সংক্রান্ত মূল দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমা ১১৭/১৯৯৯ এর কোন পক্ষ নান; সম্পূর্ণ ৩য় পক্ষ। আইনের স্বীকৃত বিধান হলো এই যে, ৩য় পক্ষের দরখাস্তের প্রেক্ষিতে কোন ডিক্রিজারী মোকদ্দমা স্থগিত হবে না।"

8. Aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 14-6-2021 the plaintiff-petitioners moved before this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

9. Mr Mohammad Eunus, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners submits that the revisional Court below committed gross illegality in setting-aside the well founded order of the trial Court below on the finding that on the prayer of a 3rd party applicant as per law a decree jari case cannot be stayed. The learned Advocate further relying on the decision reported in 23 BLC (AD) 6 submits that at the instance of a third party in a case under exceptional circumstances to secure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of Court, the Court in exercise of its inherent power under section 151 of the Code can pass an order staying all further proceedings of execution case if the petitioners have challenged the judgment and decree from which the Execution case started on the ground that the right, title and possession of the petitioners have directly been infringed. . Finally, Mr Mohammad Eunus submits that according to provisions under order 21, Rule 29 of the code of civil Procedure when a suit is pending in any Court against the holder of a decree of such Court at the instance of judgment-debtor, the court may stay execution of the decree until the pending suit has been decided. 

10. Mr Md Alim Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite parties, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment and order, which was according to him just, correct and proper. He submits that the father of the petitioner Nos. 1-6, Md Abu Taher Mia created a false deed of sale in the name of Nabuat Begum, who died and her heirs have not been substituted within 371 days and thereafter, the said Abu Taher Mia filed Title Suit No. 4278 of 2018 which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 363 of 2016 and ultimately the said suit was dismissed for default on 6-2-2017 and against which Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2017 is still pending. He further submits that the Revisional Court below rightly rejected the Revision in the following language —দরখাস্তকারী ১-৬ নং প্রতিপক্ষ ডিক্রীজারী ৯/২০০৫ সংক্রান্ত মূল দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমা ১১৭/১৯৯৯ এর কোন পার্টি নন; সম্পূর্ণ ৩য় পার্টি। আইনের স্বী গঠন করা এই যে, ৩য় পার্টির দরখাস্তের প্রেতে কোন ডিক্রিজারী মোকদ্দমা স্থিত হবে না। Finally, the learned Advocate submits that a civil Court cannot exercise its inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying the proceedings of the execution case on the prayer of a 3rd party-applicant whatsoever and, as such, the impugned judgment and order should not be disturbed. 

11. Having heard the learned Advocates for both the sides, perused the Revision application, the impugned judgment and other papers. 

12. The moot question for decision in this Rule is, whether a Civil Court in exercise of its inherent power under section 151 of the Code can pass an order staying all further proceedings of an execution case on the prayer of a third party. 

13. On scrutiny of the record, it is found that the suit property was belonged to Government and Nabuat Begum got allotment from the Government on 3-5-1966 and executed a deed in favour of her on 30-3-1968 and accordingly Government lease deed was registered on 15-4-1968 and handed over the property to her. Thereafter, the said Nabuat Begum entered into a baina deed on 31-12-1970 with the petitioner's father and consideration money was fixed amounting to Taka 20,000 out of which Nabuat Begum received Taka 19,000 from the petitioner's father in 3 installments and handed over the possession of the suit property to him. The applicant petitioner by investing money has developed the land and started residing thereon since in the year 1970 by paying all the taxes and utility bills. In this background the opposite party Nos. 2-6 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit 117 of 99 before the 2nd Joint District Judge, Dhaka against the opposite party No.1 for specific performance of contract. The learned Joint District Judge; Dhaka by his judgment dated 27-2-2003 dismissed the suit on the findings that : 
"অদ্য বিবাদীপক্ষের সাক্ষ্য গ্রহনের জন্য দিন ধার্য আছে; বাদীপক্ষ হাজির দাখিল করিলেও বিবাদীপক্ষ কোন হাজিরা দাখিল করে নাই। বাদীপক্ষের আরজি, বিবাদী পক্ষের জাব পি-ডব্লিউ ১ ও ২ এর সাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনা করিয়া প্রতিয়মান হয় যে বাদী ও বিবাদীপক্ষ পরস্পর যোগসাজসী এ মামলাটি আনয়ন করিয়াছেন।
Against the said Judgment the opposite party Nos. 2-6 filed Title Appeal No.198 of 2003, which was allowed on the basis of a solenama by compromise judgment and decree dated 9-11-2005. 

14. Against the said sole decree the decree holder plaintiffs (present opposite party Nos.2- 6) filed execution case No. 9 of 2005 and the petitioners came to know about the news of the said execution case No. 9 of 2005 and filed Title Suit No 4278 of 2008 challenging the compromise decree dated 9-11-2005 passed in Title Appeal No. 198 of 2003 and subsequently, the said suit was transferred to the court of Joint District and Arbitration Court, Dhaka and it was renumbered as Title Suit No.363 of 2016 and thereafter, the said suit was dismissed for default and subsequently, against the dismissal order the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No.10 of 2017 for restoration of the suit which is still pending and next date is fixed on 12-3-2023. Thereafter, in the Execution Case No.09 of 2005 the petitioners on 28-1-2017 filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceedings of Execution Case No. 09 of 2005 till disposal of the Miscellaneous case No. 10 of 2017 and the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka after hearing the parties stayed the execution case by his order dated 5-3-2018 till disposal of the Misc. Case No.10 of 2017. Against which the defendants filed Civil Revision No. 126 of 2018 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which was subsequently transmitted to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for disposal, who after hearing the parties by the impugned judgment and order dated 14-6-2021 allowed the Civil Revision and set-aside the order passed by the executing Court on the findings that—"উল্লেখ্য যে দরখাস্তকারী ১-৬ নং প্রতিপক্ষ উক্ত ডিক্রীজারী ৯/২০০৫ সংক্রান্ত মূল দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমা ১১৭/১৯৯৯ এর কোন পক্ষ নান; সম্পূর্ণ ৩য় পক্ষ। আইনের স্বীকৃত বিধান হলো এই যে, ৩য় পক্ষের দরখাস্তের প্রেক্ষিতে কোন ডিক্রিজারী মোকদ্দমা স্থগিত হবে না।"

15. In the case of Zainab Banu and others vs Md Misar LIddin and others reported in 23 BLC (AD) 6 it has been held that—
"The view taken in the cases of Bhame Apma (supra) and PW Fitzholmes (supra) by the respective Single Bench appears to us reasonable. The case of Paramanda Panda (supra) as relied upon by Mr Kamal-ul Alam is not at point in issue. Considering the principle of law enunciated in the above mentioned first two cases and the principle of law enunciated by this Court in the Mannujan Begum (supra), our considered view is that at the instance of a third party in a case of exceptional circumstances, i.e. to secure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of Court, a Court in exercise of its inherent power under section 151 of the Code can pass an order staying the further proceedings of an execution case in a separate suit where the decree giving rise to the execution case has been challenged. We make it very clear that a civil court cannot exercise its inherent power under section 151 of the Code at the instance of a third party as a matter of course and before exercising such power, the Court must see that one of the two conditions as stated hereinbefore must exist. And these two conditions would depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case and would entirely depend upon the wisdom of the concerned Court. We would like to observe further that in exercising the inherent power under section 151 of the Code staying the proceedings of an execution case at the instance of a third party the Court must keep in mind that the mandate of the Court as contained in a decree must not be lightly ignored or evaded to the suffering of its holder." 

16. From a plain reading of the above quoted decision, I find a clear view of law as it stands today that under the exceptional circumstances i.e. to secure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of Court, a Court in exercise of its inherent power under section 151 of the Code can pass an order staying the further proceedings of an execution case in a separate suit where the decree giving rise to the execution case has been challenged. 

17. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, I find that the present case is fully covered by the above cited decision. Therefore, I am unable to accept the findings of the Revisional Court below to the extent that execution case cannot be stayed on the prayer of a 3rd party applicant according to law. A resort to section 151 of the Code may be made in exceptional circumstances. 

18. It also appears that the opposite party No. 1 filed Title Suit No.117 of 1999 for Specific performance of contract and in the said suit the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 did not add the petitioners as party. The trial court dismissed the said suit on the clear finding that the Baina patro in favour of the opposite parties is false and collusive and thereafter the opposite party No. 1 preferred Title Appeal No. 198 of 2003 in which the parties managed to get a sole decree and in such situation the petitioners as plaintiffs challenged the sole decree passed in Title Appeal No 198 of 2003 and unless the Execution Case No.09 of 2005 arising out of compromised decree is stayed the sole purpose of the Title Suit No.363 of 2016 would be frustrated and considering this aspect, the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka stayed all further proceedings of the Execution Case till disposal of the Miscellaneous case No. 10 of 2017 which has not been at all considered by the lower revisional Court from a correct angle and thus committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

19. In view of my discussions made in the foregoing paragraphs vis-a-vis the decision reported in 23 BLC (AD) 6 it is by now clear that the instant Rule must succeed. 

20. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 14-6-2021 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No. 126 of 2018 allowing the Civil Revision and setting-aside the order dated 25-4-2018 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 9 of 2005 staying all further proceedings of the Execution Case is set-aside and that the order dated 25-4-2018 passed by learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 9 of 2005 staying all further proceedings of the Execution Case till disposal of Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2017 is restored.

21. The Court concerned is directed to hear and dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2017 (arising out of Title Suit No. 363 of 2016) as early as possible preferably within 2 (two) months from the date of receipt of this judgment. 

Let a copy of this judgment be communicated to the Courts concerned at once. 

End.

Vs.
